text_blocks.snippet: Chemical exposure can cause a wide range of symptoms depending on the substance, amount, and route of exposure (inhalation, skin contact, or ingestion). Common symptoms include skin and eye irritation, respiratory problems, nausea, vomiting, headaches, and dizziness. More severe exposures can lead to seizures, loss of consciousness, and even death.
snippet_highlighted_words: skin and eye irritation, respiratory problems, nausea, vomiting, headaches, and dizziness

list.snippet: Skin and Eye Irritation: Redness, burning, itching, rash, blistering, and blurred vision.
Respiratory Problems: Coughing, wheezing, shortness of breath, chest pain, and difficulty breathing.
Gastrointestinal Issues: Nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, diarrhea, and cramping.
Neurological Symptoms: Headache, dizziness, confusion, disorientation, loss of coordination, and seizures.
Other Symptoms: Fever, sweating, rapid heart rate, and changes in body temperature.
Long-term effects: Asthma, cancer, reproductive issues, and cognitive impairment can result from chronic exposure.
Difficulty breathing: If you are struggling to breathe or experiencing chest pain.
Burns: Chemical burns to the skin, eyes, or mouth require immediate attention.
Severe symptoms: Fainting, seizures, loss of consciousness, or confusion.
Large amounts of exposure: Ingestion or inhalation of significant quantities of a chemical warrants immediate medical evaluation.
Unknown chemical exposure: If you are unsure of the chemical involved or its potential dangers, seek medical help immediately.
Severity of symptoms: Some symptoms may appear immediately, while others can develop over time.
Individual sensitivity: People may react differently to the same chemical exposure.
Medical advice: If you have concerns about chemical exposure, consult with a medical professional or poison control center.
